chunks: The evil they perpetrated overtook them, and what they mocked has turned upon them.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when evil deeds overtake people and their mockery turns upon them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah An-Nahl illustrates the principle of 'Haaqqa' (encircling), where divine punishment not only affects the wrongdoers but specifically envelops the very mockery they directed at the prophets and divine signs. It underscores the poetic justice of retribution, where the essence of their ridicule becomes the substance of their downfall, a theme frequently cited by scholars like Al-Tabarsi to highlight the inevitability of divine truth prevailing over human arrogance.
